part.prophylaxis.title: Prophylaxis
part.prophylaxis.summary: In a quiet position, before playing your plan, ask what the opponent wants to do and take that move away. First, check the checks and captures.
ex.pf.own1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.own1.hint: What does Black want to do with the knight on a2? See which squares it would use to get out.
ex.pf.own1.solution: 1.Kd2! The king covers c1 and defends the c3 pawn, and the c3 pawn covers b4: the knight on a2 has no way out. Next, the king goes to c2 and wins the knight. After 1.Kd1?, the knight captures the c3 pawn with check and escapes.
ex.pf.own2: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pf.own2.hint: Where does the bishop on a7 want to get out? Close that exit.
ex.pf.own2.solution: 1...b6! The a7 bishop has no square: on b8, the king captures it; on b6, the c7 pawn recaptures. Next, the king goes to b7 and wins the bishop.
ex.pf.own4: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pf.own4.hint: Your king has no escape square. Before making one, look at the white king too.
ex.pf.own4.solution: 1...Re1#! The white king has no escape square either, and no white piece covers the first rank: it is a back-rank mate. With 1...h6?, the prophylactic move, White would also make a square for the king, and the mate would be gone.
ex.pf.RxgNx: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.RxgNx.hint: The black bishop on a2 is far from its own pieces. Which way does it want to come back?
ex.pf.RxgNx.solution: 1.b3! With the pawn on b3, the a2 bishop is surrounded: the c2 queen covers b1 and defends b3. If it captures on b3, 2.Qxb3, and White wins a piece for a pawn.
ex.pf.own3: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pf.own3.hint: What does White want to do with the b2 pawn?
ex.pf.own3.solution: 1...a4! White wanted to play b4 with check and drive your king away. With the pawn on a4, the b2 pawn is captured if it advances (on b4, en passant). The white king is tied to defending the b2 pawn, and your king comes in through c4.
ex.pf.mxRiC: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.mxRiC.hint: Black wants to drive your f4 bishop away with the g7 pawn. Before stopping that, see whether the position already has a tactic.
ex.pf.mxRiC.solution: 1.Ng6+! The knight gives check. If the h7 pawn captures it, the h-file opens, and 2.Qh3 is mate. With 1.h4?, the prophylaxis against the pawn going to g5, Black would trade the d6 bishop for your knight, and the chance would be gone.
ex.pf.jukuD: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.jukuD.hint: The black rook on g2 is in your camp. Which way does it want to get out?
ex.pf.jukuD.solution: 1.Rh1! The g2 rook wanted to get out through h2. Your rook covers h2 and g1, and the king defends the f2 pawn: the black rook has no way out. After 1...Rxg3+, 2.fxg3 wins the rook for a pawn.
ex.pf.LeK02: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.LeK02.hint: The bishop on b6 has few squares. After your move, check what Black threatens.
ex.pf.LeK02.solution: 1.a5! The pawn attacks the b6 bishop, which has no safe square: on c5, the b2 pawn goes to b4 and traps it. Black hits back with 1...Bh3, against the g2 pawn, defended only by the king, with the g8 rook behind. 2.g3! closes the g-file, and the a5 pawn still attacks the bishop. After 2...Bxf1 3.Bxf1, the pawn captures on b6: White gets two pieces for the rook. After 2.axb6?, the rook captures on g2 with check, and the attack belongs to Black.
